tool_input.search_target: Determine the most likely osteopathic somatic dysfunction diagnosis for T5-T10 in a 51-year-old weightlifter with restriction during toe touching and backward bending, and an anterior left transverse process at T7. Clarify how thoracic diagnosis notation encodes Type II dysfunction, flexion/extension preference, rotation, and sidebending, and map the result to choices ERRSL, FSLRR, FSRRL, ESRRL, NSRRL, ESLRR, FRRSL, NRRSL, NSLRR, FSLLR.

entities.name: T5-T10 neutral dysfunction
observations: Restriction in both toe touching and backward bending favors a neutral Type I thoracic group dysfunction.
Anterior left T7 transverse process indicates right rotation; neutral mechanics couple this with left sidebending.
The resulting diagnosis is neutral, sidebent left, rotated right; notation may be rendered NSLRR when sidebending is written before rotation.
